newsitem.title: UK: North Sea's Britannia gas field installation start.
newsitem.headline: North Sea's Britannia gas field installation start.

text.p: Work on the installation of facilities for the Britannia gas condensate field has now begun, operator Britannia Operator Ltd said in a statement on Tuesday.
Britannia, the largest undeveloped gas discovery in the U.K. North Sea, has recoverable reserves of 3.0 trillion cubic feet of gas and 145 million barrels of condensate and natural gas liquids.
On April 12, the Britannia manifold, which will control production at the subsea drilling centre 15 km west of the platform, was installed.

The installation phase now continues with the laying of the condensate export pipeline to the Forties pipeline system; laying the gas pipeline to St Fergus in Scotland; the infield bundle installation, connecting platform and manifold; the jacket installation; and six topside lifts.
In the autumn, a flotel will be delivered to support the hook-up and commissioning activities.
Production is due to start in the last quarter of 1998 with peak production capacity of 740 million cubic feet a day of gas and 70,000 bpd of condensate.

The Britannia co-venturers are Chevron UK Ltd, 30.20 percent; Conoco (UK) Ltd, 42.41 percent; Phillips Petroleum Company UK Ltd, 6.78 percent; Saga Petroleum UK Ltd, 9.01 percent; Texaco North Sea UK Co, 2.18 percent; and Union Texas Britannia Ltd, 9.42 percent. Britannia Operator Limited is jointly owned by Chevron UK Ltd and Conoco (UK) Ltd.
